newsitem.title: USA: D&P lowers senior debt rating of Aon.
newsitem.headline: D&P lowers senior debt rating of Aon.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Friday it lowered the senior debt rating of Aon Corp to double-A-minus from double-A due to an increase in financial leverage related to Aon's acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc.
The acquisition was completed earlier this year.
The addition of Alexander & Alexander enhances Aon's position as a leader in the global insurance brokerage and consulting services market, D&P said in a statement.

To fund the $1.23 billion acquisition, Aon issued $800 million of noncallable trust preferred securities that mature in 2027 and contain a five year option to defer dividend payments. D&P said that these trust preferred securities hold both debt and equity-like qualities, with long term duration and the ability to defer dividends. In addition, Aon issued $153 million of commercial paper to fund the acquisition. The remaining acquisition costs were funded through the sale of fixed income securities by Aon and Alexander & Alexander.
As of December 31, 1996, Aon's debt and preferred stock as a percent of total capital was 26 percent, D&P noted.
The rating continues to reflect Aon's market position and strong operating fundamentals, D&P said.
Shares of Aon were trading up 1-3/4 to 66-5/8.
